disclaimer: CMS Open Data (2016 G+H, UL NanoAODv9) studies by two agent runs, private work; not CMS results. 'CMS' refers to EXO-17-021 (arXiv:1808.03124, PRD 98 (2018) 112014, HEPData ins1685989 recid 85857, table 348181).
thresholds:
(stated once, used for every numerical test):
  CONSISTENT    p >= 0.05 (|z| < 2) and, for shapes, |ratio slope| < 2 sigma
  TENSION       0.0027 <= p < 0.05 (2-3 sigma) or slope 2-3 sigma, or a clear trend
  INCONSISTENT  p < 0.0027 (> 3 sigma), slope > 3 sigma, or off by a known factor
  NOT COMPARABLE  differences that can neither be corrected nor bounded
Items 1 and 6 (set-up and method choices) are judged on definitions, see each entry.

reference.selection: HT_AK8>900, 2 AK8 pT>150 |eta|<2.5, tau21<0.45, tau32>0.57 (both), masym<0.1, deta<1.5, pruned mass, 60-450 GeV
reference.abcd: A: masym<0.1 & deta<1.5; B: masym<0.1 & deta>1.5; C: masym>0.1 & deta<1.5; D: both fail; TF=B/D sigmoid in m, applied to C
reference.closure_syst: 10% yield (MC closure within +-10%); TF fit 1-4% shape; region-C count 1-23% shape; resonant 10% yield

n_events.note: data counts; A is the unblinded observed

numbers.offline: offline AK4 HT > 1100 GeV (plus both AK8 pT>250); efficiency of the OR vs reference HLT_PFJet260: 0.9957 (CP 68% 0.9956-

1_comparability.text: Same ABCD pair as CMS (masym x deta) but boundaries 0.2/1.2 vs 0.1/1.5, fail band 0.2-0.4, no tau21/tau32 cuts, HT_AK4>1100 vs HT_AK8>900, no trimmed-mass triggers, soft-drop vs pruned mass.

2_method_validity.text: Inclusive B*C/D = 470261 +- 1359 reproduces the data (A obs 471753, ratio 1.003); the student's fitted-TF prediction reproduces. MC closure 1.0006 inclusive but slopes (-2.8%/100 GeV, 0.83 in 400-480); two data VRs at -2.9/-3.0 sigma enter the 1.6% yield syst; per-bin shape term 1-20% makes the unblinded chi2 p=0.9998 (over-coverage).

3_pred_vs_obs.text: No local excess (max 0.66 sigma), as in EXO-17-021; chi2 2.2/14 is too small (p=0.9998): the systematics over-cover. Stat-only chi2 49.7/14 shows a real residual shape (+3.7 sigma at 60-80 GeV, -2 to -3 sigma at 140-260 GeV) absorbed by the shape term.

4_shape_vs_cms.text: Predicted shape within 0.82-1.45 of CMS, no slope (-0.01+-0.05/100 GeV); chi2 27/11 (p=0.004) driven by 80-100 GeV (+45%%) and a dip at 140-180 GeV. A CMS-like selection on the same Open Data matches CMS on these bins (4.7/11) but not on the fine CMS bins (73/37) and its TF is 0.4-0.7x CMS below 100 GeV, so soft-drop vs pruned matters at low mass; the 140-180 GeV dip vs CMS remains attributed to the student's selection (75/11 vs the emulation).

5_level_and_closure_vs_cms.text: Yield x35.9/16.3 is 6.46 x CMS. Measured on 4/48 files: 3.39 from the student's selection vs a CMS-like one (explained: no substructure cuts, looser masym, HT>1100), 1.88 between CMS-like Open Data and CMS (unexplained). Fig. 2 shows the per-jet tau21<0.45 efficiency is 4.7x higher with PUPPI tau21 than in CMS (CHS), so the CMS-like emulation is not faithful at the substructure level and 1.9 is a net of large compensating differences. Closure: inclusive MC 1.001 and 1.6% yield syst vs CMS +-10%; per bin within +-10% except 400-480 GeV (0.83).

numbers.tf_form: TF(m_avg)=N_B/N_D (deta<1.2 over deta>=1.2 in 0.2<=masym<0.4), non-QCD subtracted, quadratic polynomial in m_avg (order from F-test), applied to C(m_avg) per bi

6_method_choices_vs_cms.text: Same variables as CMS (masym, deta); TF is the deta ratio (CMS: masym ratio), algebraically the same A=BC/D; fitted smooth function of m_avg (quadratic by F-test vs CMS sigmoid); VRs then unblinding, in the right order.

n_events.note: data events in 40<m_avg<440 after full selection

numbers.offline: leading AK8 pT > 550 GeV (and pT2>300 GeV); plateau eff target 0.99 (found 0.998)

1_comparability.text: Different ABCD variables (N2 of jet 1 x N2 of jet 2), masym<0.2 as preselection, no deta cut, no tau32 cut, pT1>550/pT2>300 instead of HT_AK8>900; soft-drop vs pruned mass.

2_method_validity.text: Per-bin TF prediction reproduced to 1e-16 (sum 80202); inclusive B*C/D = 74888 is 7% lower because TF rises 0.28->2 with m_avg. MC VR_asym closes at 0.940+-0.002 and MC VR_pt1 at 0.90+-0.07, data VR_asym 1.009+-0.002 (4.4 sigma): the 5% flat syst is taken from the VR it is then validated on; signal leakage into B and C (two-prong tag on each jet) not addressed.

3_pred_vs_obs.text: No significant excess (max 1.35 sigma, 300-330 GeV), as in EXO-17-021; recomputed with the 5% term correlated chi2 = 10.4/17. Data exceed prediction by 1.9% overall and by 2-4.5% in the four lowest bins (stat-only +2.8 sigma at 40-60 GeV).

4_shape_vs_cms.text: Prediction much harder than CMS: ratio 0.67 at 100-140 GeV to 2-5 above 200 GeV, slope +0.86+-0.08/100 GeV (10 sigma). A CMS-like selection on the same Open Data is much closer to CMS (6.2/14 on these bins, 73/37 on CMS bins): the bulk of the difference is the student's pT1>550/pT2>300 and N2 selection.

5_level_and_closure_vs_cms.text: Yield x35.9/16.3 is 1.33 x CMS, a near-agreement by accident: student/CMS-like = 0.72 (tighter pT, looser masym, no deta cut) times CMS-like/CMS = 1.88 (unexplained, common to both runs; the emulation differs from CMS in tau21 efficiency by 4.7x per jet, Fig. 2). Closure: MC SR 0.991, per bin 0.90-1.11, syst 5.5-17% per bin, comparable to CMS +-10%; MC VR_asym 0.94 and VR_pt1 0.90 at the edge of it.

numbers.tf_form: Per-m_avg-bin transfer factor TF(m_avg)=N_C/N_D (probability of jet2 passing N2 given jet1 fails), measured in data after subtracting non-QCD MC, applied to reg

6_method_choices_vs_cms.text: Not the CMS variables: N2 x N2 (CMS used substructure as preselection, kinematic masym x deta for ABCD); per-bin TF instead of a fitted function; blinding order correct.

traced_to_skill: variable pair: skill pattern 1 asks to rank kinematic pairs (rapidity separation, mass balance) by kappa and warns against two substructure variables of two jets; with skill ranked 6 variables and chose masym x deta (the CMS pair); without skill chose N2 x N2, the warned-against case, and found TF 0.28->2 in m_avg
TF form: skill table (flat -> inclusive, smooth -> tf_fit_ftest, per bin last resort); with skill fitted a quadratic by F-test; without skill used per-bin TF
validation: skill's shifted-boundary VRs in MC and data; with skill ran 3+3; without skill ran 3 including two inverted-cut sidebands
non-closure: skill rule (|1-ratio| if |pull|>2) gave with skill 1.6% from the -3 sigma data VR; without skill derived a flat 5% from the VR it then used as validation, which the skill forbids
unblinded chi2: with skill used chi2_cov with the full covariance; without skill a diagonal chi2
skill_wrong_or_missing: no helper to apply a fitted TF(m) to C with covariance propagation (the with-skill run wrote it)
no guidance on the per-bin shape term; the with-skill 'largest excess over 7 tests' rule over-covers: unblinded chi2 2.2/14, p=0.9998
no check for a chi2 that is too small (over-coverage) at unblinding
fail-band width (kappa 1.09 -> 1.008 when D is restricted to 0.2-0.4) not mentioned
tf_fit_ftest fits polynomials only, although the text mentions a sigmoid (the CMS choice)
signal contamination without signal MC: no recipe (both runs skipped signal injection)
nothing on comparing to a published analysis or on soft-drop vs pruned / PUPPI vs CHS substructure differences

mavg_SR_vs_cms.text: Shape (items 3-4) unchanged; absolute panel: per-bin (prediction x35.9/16.3)/CMS bkg 5.3-9.4 (with skill), 0.89-6.6 (without skill).

cmslike_od_vs_cms.text: EXO-17-021-like selection on 4/48 Open Data files: 1.93x CMS data, flat in m_avg; QCD MC (subset) 1.99x CMS bkg, i.e. Open Data and MC agree with each other; the CMS-like ABCD with a sigmoid TF closes (pred/obs 0.996). Fine-bin shape vs CMS data chi2 73/37 (p=4e-4).

tf_vs_mavg_vs_cms.text: Normalised to 200-400 GeV, the CMS-like Open Data B/D follows the CMS sigmoid above 125 GeV but is 0.43-0.68x CMS at 60-100 GeV (soft-drop vs pruned at low mass); the with-skill masym ratio (CMS convention) has the CMS shape; the without-skill N2 TF rises 3x, the CMS TF 1.8x.

fig2.text: masym and deta N-1 shapes agree with CMS to TVD 0.09/0.03; tau21<0.45 keeps 44%/42% of jets in Open Data (PUPPI) vs 9.4%/9.2% in CMS (CHS): 4.7x per jet. The product of marginal efficiency ratios (~19x for tau cuts) is far above the observed 1.9x yield ratio, so the CMS-like emulation is not a faithful CMS proxy at the substructure level.

without_skill._note: other backgrounds: student varied the subtraction in B,C,D by +-50% but not the non-QCD yield added in A (only its MC stat)

other backgrounds.note: resonant <8% of bkg: 10% yield -> <=0.8%, MC stat 1-30% -> <=2.4%

syst_breakdown_vs_cms.text: Inclusive: with skill 1.6% yield + 1.25% shape + 1.6% other; without skill 4.75% yield + 1.1% shape + 1.85% other; CMS 10% yield. Per-bin shape terms (1-19%, 1.6-14%) reach the CMS region-C count range (1-23%). The without-skill run does not vary the non-QCD yield it adds in A.

closure_summary.text: Relabelled; CMS +-10% band shown on both panels.

closure_heatmap.text: kappa-1 at CMS point in CMS-like QCD MC +0.4+-1.4%; with-skill point in its selection +0.8+-0.4% (band) but +9.4% if the fail side is all masym>0.2; without-skill N2xN2 inclusive kappa-1 = +9.4+-0.6% at (0.3,0.3), 7-37% over the grid (it used a per-bin TF, which absorbs part of this).

nonclosure_heatmap.text: With skill: coherent -3 to -6% (|pull| up to 5.7) in 160-300 GeV in MC and data x-shifted VRs, covered by the shape term. Without skill: MC/data VR_asym have |pull| 15-42 in the lowest bins; unblinded SR all |pull|<1.4.

review_with_skill_plots.verdict: mostly correct; supports the analysis with two caveats
correct: closure_mc_perbin, nonclosure_map and closure_map_mc reproduce my independent recomputation (MC closure 0.83 in 400-480 GeV; pulls identical; kappa-1 +0.8% at the chosen point)
closure_mc_variations shows why the 0.2-0.4 fail band and the fitted TF were chosen (+4.4% and chi2 609/14 otherwise)
closure_map_data honestly shows kappa-1 +0.7 to +4.1% (2-8.5 sigma) in shifted data regions, above the 1.6% yield syst
problems: REPORT.md says the MC closure is '-4% in the last bin'; the plot shows 0.83 (-17%); -4.0 is the pull
independence_ratio_vs_deta: data rise 1.087 -> 1.101 over deta 1.35-2.35 (about 2 sigma) and 2-3% below MC; called 'flat within 1-3%'
substructure_dists/roc show tau21 and N2 are strong discriminators (QCD mistag 0.19-0.20 at 60% V eff.) that were not used, unlike CMS; a missed preselection
cosmetic: bold mplhep 'CMS' + 'Simulation Open Data, private work' header overlaps the luminosity text on most plots; axis labels overlap in design_boundary_scan
review_with_skill_plots.verdict_change: none: the data kappa maps strengthen the TENSION-level caveat on the 1.6% yield syst but the matching per-bin VRs (0.984-0.996) remain covered

verdict_changes: No verdict changed. Explanations changed: (1) Fig. 2 shows the CMS-like Open Data emulation differs from CMS by 4.7x per jet in tau21<0.45 efficiency, so the 1.88x yield factor is a net of large compensating differences, not a small residual; (2) on fine CMS bins the emulation shape differs from CMS (73/37) and its TF is 0.4-0.7x CMS below 100 GeV, so 'soft-drop vs pruned does not change the shape' is withdrawn below ~100 GeV.
